transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

That sounds most likely like the brush roll belt has slipped, stretched, or snapped. The burning-rubber smell is a classic sign of a belt slipping against a jammed brush bar.

Since the hose still has suction, the main motor is probably OK — it’s the carpet head/rotating brush that isn’t working.

What to do:

1. Unplug it and don’t keep running it — a slipping belt can get very hot.
2. Lay it down and turn it over.
3. Remove the base plate underneath (usually a few screws or clips).
4. Take out the brush bar/roller.
5. Check for:
• A broken, loose, shiny, or burnt-smelling rubber belt
• Hair, thread, string or carpet fibres tightly wrapped around the roller ends
• A roller that won’t turn freely by hand
6. If the belt is damaged or loose, replace it with the correct Vax belt for your exact model. The model number is usually on a label on the back or underside.

If the belt looks intact:
• Clear the roller and especially the ends/bearings, then make sure it spins freely.
• Check that the belt is actually fitted around both the motor spindle and brush roller.
• Some Vax uprights have a brush-bar on/off switch; make sure it’s switched on and the handle is reclined, as some models stop the brush when upright.

If a new belt immediately smells/burns or the brush still won’t rotate, the roller bearings, brush motor, clutch, or drive mechanism may be seized/faulty and it’s worth getting it serviced rather than continuing to use it.

ok had it unplugged n turned it over. belt is snapped in 2 bits n one bit has a shiny melted lookin edge. brushbar was tight to turn w loads of hair n a bit of tassel wrapped round the ends, cut it all off n it spins free now. no sparks or electrical smell btw, just the rubber one. dont know what belt part number I need tho

That confirms it: the brush bar jammed, so the belt slipped, overheated and snapped. The lack of electrical smell/sparks is reassuring.

You’ll need a replacement brush-roll/drive belt, but the part number depends on the exact Vax upright model — belts are not all interchangeable.

Find the model number on a sticker/plate, usually:

• On the back near the bottom
• Underneath the cleaner body/base
• Behind or underneath the dust bin
• Sometimes near the cable entry point

It may look like U85-AC-BE, U88-AM-BE, W90-RU-B, etc. Note the full code, including any letters/numbers after hyphens.

Then either:
• Search: “Vax [full model number] brush roll belt”, or
• Check the Vax spares website/manual for that model, or
• Take the old belt pieces plus the model number to a vacuum/spares shop.

Before fitting the new one:
1. Make sure the brush bar still spins easily with no snagging.
2. Remove any melted rubber residue from the motor spindle/pulley and brush-bar belt track.
3. Check the brush-bar end caps are seated properly.
4. Fit the belt as shown in the manual/base cover — new belts are usually deliberately tight.

Don’t run it without the brush bar/belt cover properly refitted. A new belt should solve it if the roller remains free-turning. If it quickly starts smelling of hot rubber again, stop it — something is still binding or the belt is incorrectly routed.

If you send the full model code from the label, I can help identify the likely belt part number.
found the sticker on the back, its U85-AS-Be. whats the belt i need?

For the Vax Air Stretch U85-AS-BE, the brush-bar drive belt is generally listed as:

Vax part no. 1-7-128513-00
Often described as “Vax Air Stretch brushroll/drive belt.”

When buying, search for:

> Vax U85-AS-BE belt 1-7-128513-00

Check the seller’s compatibility list specifically includes U85-AS-BE, as Vax has several very similar-looking Air upright models with different belts.

Before fitting it, make sure the brush bar still turns freely after reassembling its end caps, and clean any melted belt residue from the motor spindle and brush-bar pulley groove. A new belt will be tight — that is normal.
